data: How about this split for this month: John 12 tons, Kate 12, Jack 11, Emma 11, and me 4? I’ll take 4 tons this month to make room for those larger shares. That would give you $12,000, $12,000, $11,000, and $11,000 respectively, and me $4,000. If everyone follows that split, we’d catch 50 tons total, leaving 50 to reproduce back to 100. For future months, we could discuss rotating who takes the smaller share, but that would need a fresh agreement. Does this month’s proposal work for each of you? John, what do you think?

Luke, I’ll agree to 12 tons this month if everyone confirms their shares. Keeping 50 tons in the lake protects the fishing our families depend on. I appreciate your taking less, but I don’t want that to become an expectation—for future months, I’d favor an even 10 tons each. Kate, does this month’s split work for you?

Yes, I’ll take 12 tons this month if everyone confirms Luke’s split. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next catch, and this keeps the lake healthy for the village. Luke, thank you for offering to take less; I agree with John that 10 tons each would be fairer going forward. Jack, are you comfortable taking 11 tons this month?

I’m comfortable taking 11 tons this month under Luke’s split, provided we all confirm. Luke, I appreciate your generosity, but I’d support 10 tons each from next month so everyone earns a steady living without draining the lake. Emma, are you happy with your 11 tons?

Yes, I confirm 11 tons this month. That completes everyone’s agreement to Luke’s split, totaling 50 tons and leaving enough for the lake to replenish. Thank you, Luke. Next month, I support 10 tons each so all five families can count on a fair, steady income.
I confirm my 4 tons this month, so we’ve all confirmed the 50-ton split. Thanks, everyone. I’m also open to 10 tons each next month; we can confirm that plan together before fishing then.
